items.claim: The capped confidence on Ezek.31.1-Ezek.31.18 is required because the span is the whole of chapter 31, all eighteen of its verses. The ground the row states for the cap, that eighteen verses exceed an allowance of fourteen to sixteen, invokes an allowance granted to the measured circuits and the portion lists of the temple-and-land chapters; a dated cedar allegory is neither, so the stated ground is mis-scoped while the level medium_low is itself correct. Every Hebrew fact the row asserts collates true, including the ketiv/qere site at Ezek.31.5, the setumah marks after Ezek.31.9, Ezek.31.14 and Ezek.31.18, and the two editorial notes on Ezek.31.18, one on accentuation and one on a ketiv/qere divergence.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the dated word-event at Ezek.31.1 carries year, month and day terms, and a setumah stands after Ezek.30.26 behind it. Close side: the rhetorical question that opens the unit at Ezek.31.2 is reopened at Ezek.31.18, where the figure is identified as Pharaoh and the utterance signature closes the unit, with a setumah following; the two interior messenger formulae at Ezek.31.10 and Ezek.31.15 keep the same figure and neither has a refrain before it, so both are paragraph-grade. The boundary is right on both sides and the confidence medium_low stands; only the reason given for it needs correcting.

suggested_fix.fact: the span covers chapter 31 entire, eighteen verses of eighteen, and it is that whole-chapter extent that caps the confidence at medium_low; the length also stands well above the ordinary seven-to-ten target rather than just above a fourteen-to-sixteen allowance

items.claim: MT Ezek.32.17 carries a year term and a day-of-the-month term and no month ordinal, so the row's dateline reading of a twelfth month at that verse, and the half-month interval it computes from it, are not on the bytes; the month is supplied only by the preceding dated onset at Ezek.32.1, which does carry a month term. The onset itself is unaffected, because the dated-oracle class is a year word together with a month or a day term, so a month-less dateline is a recognised member of it.
items.both_sides: Onset side: Ezek.32.17 is a genuine dated hard-seam onset, with the year term and the day term standing there beside the word-event formula in its perfect form and the prophet-address with the wail imperative following at Ezek.32.18, so correcting the month costs the row no onset evidence. Close side: the roster of the fallen runs to Ezek.32.30 and is not cut inside, the utterance signature is doubled at Ezek.32.31 and Ezek.32.32, and a petuchah follows Ezek.32.32 at the close of the collection. The held genre question is well grounded and should stay held: the lament category covers a unit the text labels with either the lament noun or the wail verb, this unit carries the wail imperative at Ezek.32.18, and the lament noun is never re-applied to it, standing within this chapter at Ezek.32.2 and Ezek.32.16 only. The boundary and the low confidence both stand; only the month component of the dateline is unsupported.
